name: agent-avatars
description: A pixel-art crew for Claude Code: distinct personalities and worlds with their own pastimes, gatherings and real-event reactions. Choose cozy, chaotic or adventure behavior and how lively the scene feels.

behavior.title: Behavior
behavior.description: Cozy: gentle workshop habits. Chaotic: oversized tools and theatrical mishaps. Adventure: maps, lanterns and expedition gear. Changes the performance, never agent decisions.

liveliness.title: Liveliness
liveliness.description: Quiet: subtle movement and rare antics. Normal: occasional personality moments. Lively: expressive movement and more frequent antics. Independent of behavior.

skin.title: Character
skin.description: Which character the agents are. Mixed gives every agent a different one.

scene.title: Scene
scene.description: The world the characters live in. Auto follows the character.

sky.title: Background
sky.description: Transparent shows only the scenery; filled paints a sky behind it.

names.title: Agent names
names.description: static: the task text as is. short: trimmed to the point, free. ai: a small model coins a name (one small request per agent, uses your quota).

thoughts.title: Speech bubbles
thoughts.description: static: reading/searching/running. action: what the agent just did (read file.rs, $ cargo test), free. ai: a small model sums up the last actions (a small request every ~12 s per working agent, uses your quota).

sound.title: Sounds
sound.description: Short 8-bit blips when an agent appears, finishes, fails or asks you a question. Off by default. The engine plays them with afplay, so this works on macOS only.

events.title: GitHub events
events.description: Fireworks and confetti when the session receives a pull request merge from GitHub, and sad robots when CI fails. Only the kind and outcome of the event are read.

look.title: Light or dark
look.description: auto follows your Claude Code theme (and the system, if the theme says auto); dark and light force the colours of clouds, stars and snow.
